title: DPS Confirms Border Patrol Agent Fatally Shot Laredo Father Ernesto Quintana on Nov. 2
excerpt: The Texas Department of Public Safety has confirmed that Ernesto Quintana, a 44-year-old Laredo father of five, was shot and killed by a U.S. Border Patrol…
content:
The Texas Department of Public Safety has confirmed that Ernesto Quintana, a 44-year-old Laredo father of five, was shot and killed by a U.S. Border Patrol agent in Webb County on Nov. 2.

The confirmation, given Nov. 18, answered questions Quintana's family had been raising for more than two weeks about how he died. Before the department's statement, investigators had not confirmed that his death was connected to a Border Patrol incident in the Aquero subdivision.

What DPS says happened

According to DPS, Border Patrol agents approached Quintana's Dodge passenger vehicle at about 2:40 a.m. near La Bota Ranch and Serenity Lane as part of an ongoing human smuggling investigation. DPS said Quintana accelerated away as agents approached, striking and injuring one agent, and a second agent fired at Quintana, killing him.

DPS said that after the vehicle stopped, one undocumented person ran away but was apprehended, and four others were taken into custody, including two who were found hiding in nearby brush and two who remained at the scene.

DPS said its troopers were not involved in the shooting. Troopers reached the scene about 3 a.m., once they learned of the shooting, according to the department.

The family's account

Quintana's daughter previously said the crashed vehicle seen at the scene was hers and that she had lent it to her father. She said she recognized it by its license plate.

"I have no words to describe what I feel right now; it's like a sad desperation, not knowing what happened to my dad," she said before DPS released its statement.

The family had said it went to DPS seeking an explanation and was told only that Quintana had been shot, that he had died, and that it had been a problem with Border Patrol, with no more information provided. The Mexican Consulate in Laredo has said an undocumented migrant was shot in the leg during the same incident and is in custody.

Investigation

The Texas Rangers are leading the investigation at the request of federal authorities. DPS said the investigation remains active and no further information is available.

What remains unanswered: the name of the agent who fired has not been released, officials have not said whether body-camera or other video of the encounter exists, and no timeline has been given for the Rangers' findings. The Webb County Medical Examiner's Office is investigating the death. No charges have been announced in connection with the shooting.
